However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. …

Here we propose a theoretical framework of photonic time crystals based on active materials with “negative” dispersion (non‐Foster materials). …

Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an efficient method for achieving such on-demand tailoring using a purely phase-only modulation scheme. The measured fidelity remains above 80% even for a 128-dimensional state, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. …

However, exploiting OAM to drive nonlinear, nonperturbative effects in solids remains challenging, especially in the mid-infrared (MIR) spectral region, key for accessing these effects in ambient air, where spatial light modulators are unavailable. …

Here, we demonstrate the coexistence of spatial and angular PSS at a monolayer WS2-SiO2/Si interface by employing vortex beams combined with weak value amplification (WVA). …

Coherent synthesis from four discrete responses per polarization channel produces two-component states with the projective geometry of a pure quantum bit. …

We explore the tweezing capabilities at fixed topology either by varying the relative weights of the orthogonally polarized components or by switching between skyrmion and bimeron polarization textures. …

We have developed a holographic system that detects and counts nanoparticles flowing through a microphysiological system without labeling. …

Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. …

articles.summary: Optical backflow in the azimuthal direction can be generated by the interference of two rotating-wave structured light beams with distinct transverse topological charges and equal intensity. Although these two momenta are not generally tied, they reverse jointly here: both acquire azimuthal backflow in a common angular sector, while their radial intervals can differ. articles.summary: A key hurdle in using optical skyrmions as information carriers in integrated photonic systems is establishing when their topological structure is preserved in propagation. Here, we demonstrate that robustness is governed by the presence of topologically stabilizing modes and rigorously establish skyrmion-number preservation in waveguides. When such modes are present, protection is ensured despite modal dispersion and coefficient variations, enabling robust high-dimensional skyrmion-based information transfer and processing.

articles.authors: Entidhar Mhawes Zghair, Seham Ahmed Hashem, Ali Mahdi Hammadi
articles.summary: Pathological chest radiographs are often assumed to be more vulnerable to channel impairments than normal ones. We simulated sending 250 NIH ChestX-ray14 radiographs from five diagnostic classes, in three payload formats sharing identical channel realizations, over a 1 km, 1550 nm free-space optical link with Gamma–Gamma fading, pointing errors and RS(255,204) coding. After an error event, diagnostic class explained 0.4–5% of the between-image variance in quality beyond grey-level statistics and JPEG size. A second, partially overlapping sample confirmed this, and a bit-level analysis explains why. …

articles.authors: Pavel A. Cheremkhin, Iuliia S. Lenkova, Daria V. Pavlenko, Vladislav G. Rodin, Anna V. Shifrina, Rostislav S. Starikov, Fedor A. Ushakov, Evgenii Yu. Zlokazov
institutions: Institute for Laser and Plasma Technologies
articles.summary: Fast optical data processing provides incredible opportunities for present-day and near-future tasks: pattern recognition, object tracking, beam shaping, development of diffractive neural networks, 3D-display and lithographic systems, etc. Digital micromirror devices (DMD) can display binary megapixel images with frame rates of tens of thousands Hz. However, grayscale images are more convenient for practical implementations. In this paper we analyzed several digital halftoning and binarization methods in search of the best one for a coherent DMD-based spatial filtering system. …

articles.summary: Spatiotemporally localized topological knots encode global connectivity within a moving space-time optical wavepacket, circumventing the requirement for spatial-only eigenmodes that extend throughout three-dimensional space-filling. In conventional modalities, this connectivity is identified directly from a scalar complex field. However, knotting optical knots with the polarization state of light proves difficult to realize for ultrafast localized wavepackets. …

articles.title: Turbulence Strength Estimation from Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams Using Multimode Fibre Speckle
articles.authors: Warwick G. C. Brown, Mitchell A. Cox
articles.summary: The strength of atmospheric turbulence governs how much the modes of a free-space optical link mix together. It is usually measured with a separate instrument or with a Gaussian probe beam, neither of which uses the beams that a structured-light link already carries. Here we show that the turbulence strength, expressed as the Fried parameter, can be estimated directly from multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams without knowing which modes are present. …

articles.title: Projector Time Map Calibration for Event-based Structured Light
articles.authors: Buu-Hoang-Lam Le, Kota Mizutani, Shohei Nobuhara
articles.summary: Existing event-based structured light obtains a dense projector-camera correspondence from the timestamp of an event. It assumes that the projector scans a parallel raster and that the sensor timestamps each pixel independently, and we show that neither assumption holds. We obtain the correspondence from a temporal code that identifies the projector pixel directly and therefore needs no prior calibration, we calibrate the projector time map from the same recording, and we recover the geometry of the system and the offsets between its clocks by a spatio-temporal self-calibration in a preamble of a few seconds that needs no reference object and no second camera.

articles.title: Free-Space Excitation of Frozen Waves and Topological Edge States in Graphene at a Time Interface
articles.authors: Shivaksh Rawat, Samyobrata Mukherjee, Jeffery Allen, Monica S. Allen, Gennady Shvets
articles.summary: Time-varying two-dimensional materials, such as graphene under ultrafast photoexcitation, offer a promising platform for engineering temporal interfaces for electromagnetic waves. Rapidly promoting valence electrons to the conduction band generates a high-energy, non-thermal hot-electron population that subsequently thermalizes with the pre-existing thermal electron population. We study the excitation of plasmonic modes in graphene by the time interface created by ultra-fast photoexcitation using a graphene electron-transport model that is self-consistently coupled to electromagnetic simulations. …

articles.summary: To meet the demand for miniaturized, low-power high-voltage pulse power supplies for time-of-flight mass spectrometers (TOF-MS), we designed a compact half-bridge push-pull pulse power supply. The power supply achieves a frequency range of 1-100 kHz, a maximum output voltage of 800 V, pulse-width adjustment in 0.1 μs steps, and a power consumption of ∼10 W. Electrical characterization shows that the rise time is less than 10 ns, overshoot is below 5%, amplitude and period stability are excellent, and the synchronization between positive and negative pulses is reliable. …

articles.title: Scattering of Ince–Gaussian beams by a homogeneous isotropic dielectric sphere
articles.authors: Maryam Alshehhi, Ghalyah Alsereidi, Hamad Alkhoori
articles.journal: Journal of the Optical Society of America A
articles.summary: Scattering of Ince-Gaussian (IG) beams by a homogeneous dielectric sphere is investigated using a volume integral equation formulation solved numerically using the method of moments. The incident IG beams are characterized by their mode indices, parity, beam waist, semi-focal distance, and polarization state. The scattering characteristics are analyzed in terms of directivity, normalized total scattered power, and normalized absorbed power. Validation of the formulation is established through comparisons with limiting cases, including plane-wave and Laguerre-Gaussian-beam incidences. …

articles.title: DART-SIM: a self-supervised super-resolution reconstruction method robust to structured light parameters
Low-loss spatial phase modulation of mm-waves via optically-tunable coupling
articles.authors: White GN, Hooper IR, Penketh H, Burton F, Phillips DB, Hendry E
articles.summary: Efficient phase modulation at mm-wave and THz frequencies is an ongoing challenge. Here, we introduce a method for high-resolution dynamic spatial phase modulation of mm-waves, via selective photo-activation of a silicon-based resonant metasurface. In contrast to conventional methods of regulating the phase of reflected waves by shifting the resonance frequency of a modulator, we control the resonant coupling strength to realise low-loss binary phase modulation. We demonstrate a system operating at a wavelength of 6 mm, realising dynamically encoded holograms enabling focussing, beam steering, multi-casting and orbital angular momentum mode generation. …
